source.quote: Greetings travelers and welcome back to Goldbound, the challenge series where our rogue Goldilocked is exploring Azeroth by unlocking one zone at a time. In last episode, we left off in the Badlands with a mailbox clear and a cash stack of 215,000 gold, which means we're about 45,000 gold away from the wild token and a new zone spin. So, let's waste no time and get into a mini mailbox clear. So, as you can see here, I did clear out and mail over my transmog alt sales just so we can see it all here in one place nice and quickly. The backlog alt, I moved a couple lock button and bear skin rugs for about 6,000 each. And the Badlands alt, 8.7 thousand gold, which is more than we cleared before with almost 6,000 gold of that being the Digmaster Shovel Flange Mining Pickaxe. A good sale to see, but still, transmog has been slow moving recently. On top of that, for trade goods here, we have a few of the Badlands skins and herbs, but not too much. So, let's get this all looted up and see where we're actually sitting.

source.quote: All right. So, we're up to 249,700 gold, which is just about 8.5k short of the token. We better get farming. And what better way to get the last couple thousand gold than raw gold farming in new Aldor Inn, Legacy of Tier. We already optimized this one quite a bit last episode, at least as far as a raw gold farm goes, so it should just be about two hours of raw farming getting about 4.5k raw per hour to get to the token. I think this is the best move right now because even though trade goods could be a higher gold per hour, we not only have to farm the items, we have to list them, wait for them to sell, and then once sold, wait for the mail to be delivered from the auction house. So, I think from a speed perspective, this is the best bet. So, while the gold steadily trickles in from the raw gold farm, let's talk about what zones we can spin once we get our hands on a new token. And this isn't actually much different from our last zone spin at all because the current new zone of Badlands doesn't actually open up access to any other zones. So, really, it's the same wheel with one less zone. So, over on Kalimdor, we're still rolling between Barrens and Thousand Needles. And over here on Eastern Kingdoms, we still have Deadwind Pass, Arathi Highlands, and Twilight Highlands up for grabs. I'm kind of preferring Deadwind Pass, which is crazy, but this zone has been on the randomizer for 12 consecutive zone spins without being hit. But, uh well, we're definitely getting raw gold here. I hit the 258,000 gold, but as you can see, the token is climbing by about the same amount of gold that we can farm. We have a moving target. So, while I continue to farm raw gold for the next token spin, let me tell you what the sponsor of today's episode, which is kind of fitting as I'm farming dungeons in wow.

source.quote: But like I said, in addition to the raw gold coming in, we have some auctions moving, which does mean that we're ready to do the spin and roll a new zone. And let's waste no time in getting after it. Okay. So, we rolled the Arathi Highlands, which wasn't on one of my top cards, but there are some cool aspects to it, I think. So, let's get over there and get after it. Now, one big thing about Arathi Highlands is that it's another Zidormi zone, kind of like Blasted Lands, where we can phase between two versions of the zone. So, for starters, we have the classic or technically the Cataclysm version of the zone. This is the standard version with refuge point, Witherbark Village, and Hammerfall. Pretty much all the regular graphic design. But it is a little bit buggy, and some of the mobs do jump all over the place. But then, when talking to Zidormi, we can actually turn the version of the Highlands over to that of during the Fourth War, aka the Battle for Azeroth. Oh, yeah. This version of the Highlands is pretty similar, but we have BFA textures and a whole different angle to explore. Some of the sites are still there, some of the mobs are the same, but a lot of them are different.

source.quote: We're really here for the gold. And there is one gold angle on the warfront rares, battle pets. And there's actually quite a few that can drop some battle pets. They're relatively standardized here as far as market values. All the battle pets from the rares here, about nine of them, have the same values and drop rates. With a 15% drop and a market value between 5 and 12,000 gold. But, with a drop rate of 15% and nine rares per reset to kill, we have a pretty good chance of getting at least one per clear. Like the Aldrusian Sproutling, which is dropped from the Branch Aldrus, or the Fuzzy Creepling from Venomous. That being said, it is kind of hard to target a specific one since you can only kill them once or twice a month. But that being said, the most valuable pet actually drops from Ragebeak. It's called the Ragepeep, noted as part owl, part bear, part stag, and a solid market value of around 12,000 gold. But honestly, these guys are called rare spawns, but they're basically forced respawn quest named mobs. So the move is to definitely come here and just clear out all of the rares in one swoop for a chance at all the battle pets, mounts, and transmog. Not to mention, you technically can get some toys from them, too. And as far as our first clear here, well, no dice on the mounts or the battle pets. We got kind of unlucky there since they're all relatively high drop rates, but we are walking away with a few pieces of the set. The Seventh Legionnaire bracers, chest, and legs. So if we end up doing another run at the rares, we may walk away with some gold. But what about the rest of the mobs here in the BFA version of the zone? While exploring here, it is kind of a mixed bag. The vast majority of the mobs out here have completely grey-washed loot tables where basically all they can drop are some vendor greys and raw gold. That being said, the raw gold is not negligible and in most cases is over one gold each. And on top of that, there are a few exceptions to the grey drop rule, and it's trade goods. So some of the beasts do drop BFA level meat, Kul Tiran meat. And then some of the humanoids can drop BFA level cloth, tidespray linen, and deep sea satin.

source.quote: Aside from those two exceptions, the BFA version of the zone is kind of a sea of vendor greys and then rares that we can only kill once per two weeks or so. But at the moment, Alliance currently controls the zone, and that means Stormguard Keep is full of Alliance citizens, NPCs. So let's go take a look. And by far the biggest thing I found here amongst the MPCs, well, there's profession trainers and they have a Battle for Azeroth level training. And travelers, we just so happen to have a tailoring trainer. Now, I did not expect this in this zone at all, but I'm going to say right now, it's a welcome sight. And I think between the mobs dropping BFA cloth and there being a tailoring profession trainer here, we may just be able to craft some new bags. So, looking into the trading list, I actually think it's possible crafting the bags only requires level 50 tailoring and to get there, all we need is tidespray linen and deepsea satin to level up and then the bags themselves require the same. And the deepsea bags we could craft here are 30 slot bags, which is over eight slots per bag improvement over our current embersilk bags. This is definitely worth the mini side quest. So, I've ran around a little bit testing out killing some of the humanoids for farming cloth and deepsea satin in particular seems to be a pretty low drop rate. On my first loop around the zone killing every single humanoid, I only got three, but I think with how later expansions work, if I pick up the culturist tailoring right away, it may improve the drop chances of the cloth. I mean, it's worth trying at least, especially because we kind of need to speed run this craft and get the recipe trained before the Horde takes control of the zone because once the Horde and Hammerfall have control of Arathi, well, then we have no more trainers. So, let's get farming and min-maxing this cloth grind. The target, of course, four bags and each bag takes 15 tidespray linen and 30 deepsea satin to craft. So, we need about 60 linen and 120 satin. The linen though is definitely a higher drop rate, so it's really the deepsea satin that we need.

source.quote: There's a ton of Witherbark trolls here, headhunters, witch doctors, axe throwers, and between the caves and the groups around, there's quite a few mobs to kill before the anti-hyper spawn mechanics kick in. Once they do though, we can move up north and to the east to Dambrie's Farmstead for a few of the syndicates here, clearing them all out. Once they're cleared, heading over to the Goblin Mine to take down some of the goblin miners for a few more. I found the best route here was only doing half the mine, pretty much just only the goblins on the surface. Otherwise, you go for a pretty long run through the mine and the density isn't that great. And just the surface is long enough to go back to the ogres and have fresh tables. This big loop definitely isn't as AFK as a sit in hyper spawn type of farm, but it definitely does get the trick done and the raw gold angle here is actually pretty decent. So, after a few hours of farming and testing, here's the stats. For straight raw gold vendor selling looted, we're pulling in about 1,500 gold per hour here. It's not exactly ultimate legacy of tier, but it's pretty good as far as raw gold goes. Then for tidespray linen, we're getting about 650 per hour. Mind you, this is definitely increased once we swapped over to tailoring, so it's confirmed that does increase the drop rates. And at one gold each, that's about 650 gold per hour in just linen, but we may be able to improve that by processing further. And after the optimization for farming multiple packs, I'm actually getting 32 Deepsea Satin per hour, which is great because that's over one bag per hour, which adds on another 140 gold per hour for the actual cloth. So, as far as total cloth value per hour, we're looking at 800, but when combined with the raw gold, it makes this humanoid killing loop about 2,300 gold per hour, which isn't breakneck speeds by any means, but it's definitely better than I thought, and we need to farm it anyways to get these bags, so I'm just going to go ahead and lock in for a bit and farm with the rest. And while we have a little bit of tidespray linen and the trainers are still here before Horde takes over, I can actually just level up my tailoring by crafting tidespray linen bandages most of the way. This is by far the cheapest and the least material-intensive way to level it up, which it does get us to level 50, and we can actually learn the recipe to make our first bag. Luckily, Amy Hardy here, the tailoring supply vendor, does sell the BFA level thread, the nylon thread, that we need to make these crafts. So, look at that. The first Deepsea bag obtained, and the 30 bag slots is no joke. We've moved up from six slots to eight slots to 16 slots to 22 slots, and now 30 slot bags.

source.quote: Why the bracers? Well, they're just the cheapest to craft of all the tailoring greens. They only require 10 tidespray linen. So, with 1,800 linen, I can craft 180 of them before dropping tailoring for enchanting for a classic tailoring enchanting shuffle. So, the baseline cost on crafting these bracers is pretty much the opportunity cost of what you would get for selling the linen. So, 10 gold for the tidespray linen, plus we have to account for the nylon thread, which six thread at 60 silver each is 3.1 gold in thread per bracer. So, as long as the average disenchant value is higher than 13.1 gold, we'll be in the green. So, there we go. 180 bracers crafted. I did have to do a couple bank runs because although we have big bags, we don't have 180 slots to spare. But, here it is. Back to Stormgarde to drop tailoring and grab enchanting. And then, the slow but enjoyable process of disenchanting. I am using TSM Destroy here just for ease of clicking, but be careful if you use this because it's kind of easy to accidentally disenchant an item you don't want. Maybe a viable green transmog item or two if they happen to be in your inventory. Also, if you're wondering why I'm not doing this on my crafting alt that I got from Dun Morogh Golden Path, well, on him, I have pretty high-leveled blacksmithing and leatherworking and invested quite a few hours to source all the materials to level it up. Not to mention, I have learned quite a few rare recipes for blacksmithing and leatherworking on him.

source.quote: Now, this isn't terrible, but for the profit here of 982 gold, it did take me about 30 minutes in total processing time, which comes out to just under 2,000 gold per hour. A cool farm, no doubt, but we definitely have to explore more to try to find a higher gold per hour farm if we want to get that token anytime soon. And looking around the rest of Stormgarde, it's kind of dead as far as further profession farms. Without access to BFA herbs or ores, the alchemy and blacksmithing trainers are kind of just red herrings and we can't do much with them. So, I do think it's time to talk to Sidormi and see if the classic version here can offer any better values. Now, as far as the classic zone goes, I think the angle will be similar to a lot of the previous zones with a mix of gold coming between steady farms like skinning, mining, herbalism, and then some more volatile farms like transmog, rares, and perhaps even lockboxes. But, like always, we have to start somewhere and because my instinct is that it might not be amazing, I'm actually going to start with testing skinning. This way, if dual gathering ends up being the best method, then down the road, I can just spend more time doing that and not unlearning 300 level mining or herbalism to test some skinning farms. So, excuse me while I power level up my skinning one zone down in the Wetlands at the hyper spawn farm, which is just the fastest way from one to 300 skinning. And there we go, back to Arathi because there's a lot to skin in this zone. For the most part, the zone has a pretty wide spawn of skinnable mobs, most of which are assorted types of raptors, but since there aren't any really small tight-knit groups of one type of mob, the route has to be a near full zone clear, jumping between raptors. So far, I haven't found anything that resembles a mini hyper spawn of three specific mobs or any particular group that can be killed over and over. That being said, there is a group of raptors down in the south of the zone, the Highland Fleshstalkers, that we definitely want to tag in this rotation because on their basic loot tables, they have raptor hide. This crafting reagent used to drop from all of the raptors in the zone, but after the cataclysm, the tables got a little bit bugged and now they only really drop off these guys, so we may as well tag them when we can. The hide itself is worth about 10 gold, but it's only used in a few niche transmogs, so only about 50 sell per day. Definitely an item you want to have stocked, but not one you want a thousand of. On top of the trade goods here, the beasts in Arathi are in the heavy leather and medium leather band, with a bias towards medium leather. As far as the spread, looking at the results of an hour of farming here, it is actually strongly biased towards medium leather. So I pulled in 254 medium leather, which combined has a market value of about 1,100 gold, and for heavy leather, I only got 62. So about 461 gold worth of heavy. Now the downside here, because this is mostly medium leather, we actually only got two heavy hides from the whole hour. This is usually the big ticket item that can really move the needle on classic skinning farms, but with only two, it only adds 200 gold to the hour. If this was higher, it could have been a lot better. And as far as medium hide, we got 24. And the beasts also give us some trash, which came out to about 31 gold. So skinning in the classic version here gives us a grand total of 1,800 gold per hour.

source.quote: And right now, I can snag some saber leggings as well as the guardsman's belt. And actually, the formula to enchant gloves for classic enchanting. I think that this one is just a base improvement to the skill level and not a faster gathering speed, but all of these have some pretty respectable values between 500 gold and 3,000 gold. And likewise, down in refuge point, we have a few NPCs worth chatting to as well. First up, Hammond Carwin, a tradesman who has a few recipes on his wares as well. There's nothing too crazy here, couple hundred gold on the auction house, but definitely worth grabbing. And then behind us, something kind of interesting, a PvP vendor. Now, this is all purchasable with marks of honor and is soulbound, so not a gold farm. Not to mention, it's also not an upgrade because everything here is item level 16, so maybe a little bit of a transmog angle for goldy. And perhaps more of note is his friend, Radulf's letter, the Arathi Basin Battlemaster. This guy, well, he actually unlocks our very first PvP battleground, Arathi Basin. I mean, worst case, it'll be a good spot for rep farming. And best case, well, we might just be able to sneak out a cheeky gold farm here. But more on that later, because even if the battleground is good for gold, the queues do look quite long and we haven't really found any super reliable gold farms here yet in Arathi, so it's time to dust out the old reliable, dual gathering. So while we wait in queues, let's farm up and level up mining and herbalism. With the herbs and ores in this zone, I think about 200 skill in each should get us enough skill to gather everything here fully. Now, as far as herbs and ores go in Arathi, it's kind of interesting. We do get the same types of herbs and ores in both versions of the zone, so no change there, but we may able to use a different version to our advantage later. As far as ore though, we are getting primarily iron ore, which has some pretty solid values, but also some sprinkles of tin and mithril as well. On top of that, a few of the rarer spawns of silver and gold. So, pretty solid ore values all around. Then for herbs, we have a wide variety in the zone, but the top contenders are definitely goldthorn with its juicy market value and grave moss, another juicy market value. Although grave moss only spawns in one extremely small location down around the map by Stormgarde Keep in the graves, and it does actually spawn here in both versions of the zone, but on the BFA version, it actually spawns outside of the wall, so a bit of a weird coding bug there. On top of the heavy hitting herbs though, we do have some moderate value from fadeleaf and Cadgar's whisker with a few even lower value herbs sorted in there as well. But for this one, there's a few different types of this dual gathering farm that I do want to do.

source.file: 035 - I Went Looking For WoW’s Forgotten 9,999,999g Item - Goldbound Ep.34.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/035 - I Went Looking For WoW’s Forgotten 9,999,999g Item - Goldbound Ep.34.en-orig.txt
source.quote: So, even though the zones have the same types of herbs and ores, it's actually a completely different phase of the zone. So, I can clear out all of the nodes on the classic version, then hop over to BFA for a brand new fresh set of herb and ore nodes. And in theory, this should massively increase our yield. So, the results? Oh, yeah, it does. So, after testing this again swapping and grabbing every single node, the results speak for themselves. With our spread of herbs and ores here, we're bumped up to 6,200 gold per hour on this test. Not too shabby at all, and by almost a factor of three, our best farm in the zone. But, there might be one better way. So, I'm wondering, what if we dual gather in both versions of the zone, but only selectively grab the herbs and ores that are worth quite a bit of gold? Things like iron, mithril, silver, gold, leaving out the tin, and then getting herbs like goldthorn, grave moss, and fadeleaf, while leaving out the wild steelbloom and bruiseweed. In theory, I think this may increase the yield even further. On testing, though, there is definitely a downside. What I'm doing here to mark the viable nodes is using GatherMate 2, an add-on that tracks where I gathered them before, but even with this helping, the farm itself is quite a bit more attention-intensive when constantly going back and forth on the mini-map to see which node it is and if I want to grab it. Plus, I suppose due to flying farther between nodes, our actual gold yield dropped down as well, down to about 5,500 gold per hour, which is still an improvement over single-zone dual gathering. So, the conclusion? Well, for a steady gold farm, we do want to dual gather, grab every single node, and swap between BFA and classic versions to double up on our nodes. Roger that. And just in time, queue pop for Wrathion base. Let's see how this one goes. And actually, it looks like our gear is scaled up to about 190 item level. Not bad. Although I did think a few extra pieces might help. We're missing a few, and I did manage to snag this Huntsman's Chestpiece from one of the rares in the classic version while dual gathering or on those rares down the road. But first, let's see if we can find a gold farm here. At the very least, I can try and do my team a solid by capping the flag and trying to defend it. Looking at health pools though, even with the item level scaling, I am still 1/2 1/3 of everybody's level, so I don't like my odds.

source.quote: So, true sales are probably closer to 1 mil, and fast sales might be a bit lower, but it is a serious item, and one we definitely want to farm. So, to farm it, there are a few options. We can just kill all the exterior trolls, AFK for 6 to 8 minutes until one responds, and do it over and over, which is not a bad low-intensity farm. Or, we can use some of the mobs around them to increase the value, and kind of kill time while they're responding. A more active farm. To do this, we basically just pickpocket and kill all the ogres outside and inside of the mound, plus grabbing any herbs and ores we see along the way as well. The actual loot tables for these mobs aren't too crazy. I'm really just killing them so they respond with fresh pockets, but the pickpocket tables actually do have some angles. First up, they all have lucky charms at a decent drop rate, so we can get some good trade good value from those. Plus, they do have battered junk boxes.
